“While I was physically present with my family, mentally I was absent”: why a laid-off Singapore mum of two tested an online store with a mentor

Fierra, 35, gave an online store a 3-month test with a mentor and kept job hunting as her fallback. Learn how she became a full-time entrepreneur who now works 2 to 3 hours a day so she can spend more time with her kids, and how she got started.

By Ecomwarts·October 22, 2026·9 min read

Fierra's workday started before her kids were properly awake.

Teams and email were open first thing. The day's problems were already hers.

For 15 years as a project manager in Singapore, that was normal. So was packing the laptop for family holidays.

“Even on holidays, I had to bring my laptop to attend issue resolution calls with customers.” Her kids had their mum at the table. Her attention was with the client.

Then, after 15 years, the job ended

She worked about 40 hours a week, and the extra hours went unpaid. At 35, she was laid off.

She had two young kids, “liabilities and responsibilities”, and a small severance that would cover the basics for a few months.

“It was scary. I had a small severance payout... so time was of the essence.”

She had two options. Find another job, and accept the same trade. Or learn new skills and build the business she had always wanted.

She wasn't starting blind. She had tried dropshipping six or seven years earlier, so she knew the model was real.

So she set a limit: “I gave myself a timeframe of 1 to 3 months to test this business model...”

She kept job hunting as her fallback. Her husband backed the plan, even before the store had made anything.

What she tested: an online store, with someone checking her work

Dropshipping works like this: you run the online store and the ads, and a supplier holds the stock and ships each order.

No shop to rent. No boxes in the house. It could run from home, around school hours.

What she wouldn't do was piece it together alone. Time was the one thing she couldn't waste. She wanted a mentor “...instead of wasting time searching through random YouTube videos or Reddit threads.”

She found Rayston Heem, founder of Ecomwarts, through his YouTube tutorials and his students' stories.

“Seeing testimonials from other successful students made me ask why I couldn't achieve the same results.”

AI tools now help with parts of the build. They don't make the decisions. She still had to learn the work and make the calls.

Even with her earlier attempt, it took her two weeks to a month to feel comfortable in Shopify and Facebook Ads Manager again. The early days took many hours. They got fewer as she gained experience.

The sacrifice she names is focus: “Dedicating full focus days to building the store was key.” Her first product got the store moving. She has since added a second.

Her numbers, and the part most case studies leave out

Thumbnail from Fierra's July 2026 interview on Rayston Heem's YouTube channel. The headline on it is the video's title. Her own figure and dates are below.

Fierra reports $318,000 USD in revenue between mid-March and July 8, 2026.

Fierra's figure is her own, from a video interview on July 8, 2026. It is revenue, not profit, and Ecomwarts has not checked it. Her result is not typical. The typical outcome is no income.

What she values more: today her mornings go to the business, and to herself. Her afternoons start at the school gate. The rest of the day is with her kids.

In June 2026, the family went to China. “I did not need to check my phone for work chats or emails, allowing me to be 100% present with my family.”

That is her experience, not a promise. The store still takes her work.

Is this right for someone like you?

Fierra had doubts too: “I thought it looked unrealistic at first as well.” What settled it for her was that she had tried the model years before.

Her story differs from most readers' in real ways. She had tried dropshipping before, she had severance to cover the basics, and her husband backed the test. It may suit you if:

✓
You have a job and very little spare time — Fierra planned her test with a time limit and a fallback.
✓
You want to build something for your family — Her reason was to be present for her kids.
✓
You have a budget for ads — Running a store means paying for ads while you test. Without that budget, it won't suit you yet.
✓
You're ready to do the work — Even with AI tools, it took her weeks of relearning and full-focus days. If you're hoping for results without the work, it won't suit you.
✓
You'd like to see the work before you decide anything — That's what the workshop is for. The paid program at the end is optional.
